title: Tiny sprint seeding dossier
content:
Context:
This is a personal scratch dossier capturing a few tiny-sprint ideas to improve first-time user success for the Hosted API onramp. Goals are pragmatic: increase first-week active usage, reduce time-to-first-successful-call, and create 1–2 low-effort A/B experiments we can ship inside a micro-sprint (3–5 days).

High-level hypothesis:
- If we reduce cognitive friction in the first 10 minutes of signup (sample code + validated prompt + one-click run), then more teams will run meaningful calls and convert to second-week usage.

Priority levers to test (ranked):
1) One-click sample flow for `text.generate` (no config surfacing)
   - Landing page has single language toggle, model dropdown defaulted to a lightweight verified model, and a single "Run sample" CTA that executes in-console.
   - Metrics: percent of new accounts that run sample within 10 minutes, median time-to-first-call.

2) Tiny guided prompt pack (3 curated prompts) surfaced in the console + SDK quickstart
   - Each prompt has: short title, expected tokens, and a small expected output preview.
   - UX: inline copy that says "Best for: prototypes / demos / tests" to lower expectation mismatch.
   - Metrics: reuse rate (clicked prompt -> run), subsequent calls in 24h.

3) Console quick-feedback micro-hint after first call (success / tips for next step)
   - If user receives valid tokens, surface a short nudge: "Nice! Try a streaming response or call with function-calling to integrate this into an app." + 1-click link to create a new route.

Constraints / guardrails:
- Minimal infra touch: use hosted-model variants we already support; no new back-end model onboarding.
- Privacy: don't capture sample payloads in logs beyond telemetry counts (check privacy checklist).
- Scoping: first sprint avoids subscription/billing changes. Focus purely on P0 UX and telemetry.

User stories (rough):
- As a brand-new developer, I want to press one button and see a sample output so I can verify the API works without reading docs.
- As an engineering lead evaluating Redwood, I want simple demo prompts that showcase latency and cost so I can present to my team.
- As an SDK user, I want the quickstart snippet to match the console sample so I can copy/paste easily.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- New-accounts funnel: console exposes "Run sample" visible on first visit (desktop + mobile).
- Click -> sample run completes within our normal SLO (99% success within 3s perceived).
- Telemetry emitted: sample_run (user, model, time-to-first-token), prompt_pack_item (id, clicked).
- No PII stored in sample_run payloads.

Success metrics (primary):
- Increase in 7-day retention for new accounts that ran sample vs control (target: +8% absolute).
- Median time-to-first-successful-call drops to < 5 minutes for new accounts (current baseline ~12m).
- Weekly active calls from new accounts increases by 20% in cohort.

Experiment matrix (ideas):
- Variant A: One-click sample only (control: existing quickstart)
- Variant B: One-click sample + guided prompt pack
- Variant C: One-click sample + guided prompt pack + post-call micro-hint
- Track cohorts by traffic source (signup via docs vs signup via quickstart link).

Operational notes / tech dependencies:
- Frontend: small console UI modal + sample runner (React component) — owner: @Mateo
- Backend: use existing run endpoint with a `sample=true` flag to bypass quota prompts for new accounts — owner: Platform (TBD)
- Telemetry: add new events and ensure filtering in analytics (inc GA + internal events) — owner: Lina
- Legal/privacy: quick check to confirm sample templates contain no copyrighted content (ask compliance).

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Do we expose model selection? (Trade: trust vs control. For MVP, default to a verified small model and allow an advanced dropdown hidden behind "change").
- Should we pre-warm a tiny dedicated instance for sample runs to reduce cold-start noise? (Cost trade-off.)
- What is the right UX for mobile console? Keep parity but simplified layout.

Mini rollout plan (3 sprints):
- Sprint 0 (planning, infra + telemetry hooks) — 3 days
- Sprint 1 (frontend + sample runner + 1st prompt pack) — 5 days
- Sprint 2 (experiment gating, analytics dashboards, tweak prompts) — 4 days
- Quick followup A/B iterate based on week-1 signals.

Notes to self / low-priority ideas (parking lot):
- Quickstart email nudge sent 24 hours after signup with link to replay sample (if they didn't run).
- Lightweight badge in repo README generator: "Built with Redwood — ran sample" to encourage demos.
- Prompt pack marketplace idea (much later).

Immediate TODOs (next 24–48h):
- Sync w/ @Mateo for component sketch (today)
- Open ticket RED-1127 and link this doc, include telemetry checklist (tomorrow)
- Quick chat with legal to confirm sample templates (by EOD Thu)

Slack snippets to use in outreach: 
- "Trying a tiny experiment for 1-click sample runs — low infra, high signal. Want a quick pairing? @Mateo @Lina"

Rough copy for console CTA:
- Title: "Run a quick sample"
- Body: "See a working example in one click — no config required. Runs on a small verified model so you can prototype fast."
- Button: "Run sample" (secondary: "View prompt pack")

Finish note: keep the launch atomic and instrumented. If we can get clear cohort signals in 7 days we can decide whether to expand to dedicated onboarding flows.

-- end of dossier (working notes)
